claim: Humans solve small coupled parameter-design tasks almost as fast as uncoupled ones (2x2: 40 s vs 24 s, 31 coupled tasks, N=12), so Suh's strong claim that coupled designs are unworkable fails at n=2.
agent_test: Not testable as a human claim. Skip.

claim: Time to solve coupled parameter-design tasks by trial and error grows geometrically (about 3.4^n, n=2 to 5, adj R2 0.99 on means) while uncoupled grows about linearly. Replicated by Grogan and de Weck (2016): 10 groups of 3, 42 tasks, same geometric growth for highly coupled tasks. Both are MIT, both seen as abstracts or earlier ICAD text, and neither is an LLM test.
agent_test: Give the agent coupled vs uncoupled numeric tuning tasks (n=2..5) with a black-box evaluator; compare tries to target for a plain loop vs a loop that first estimates the matrix and solves it by program, at equal tokens.

claim: Frey and Hirschi (2002) has one partial replication (Grogan and de Weck 2016, a team variant at the same university); no strict independent repeat and no controlled human or LLM test of axiomatic design against another design method was found. Search was throttled, so this is weaker than a full search.
agent_test: Run the replication on an LLM agent; the result would itself be new.

claim: Goehler, Frey and Howard (2016) is a Monte Carlo study of 250 modelled architectures, not a human experiment. It finds the independence axiom holds in general only for nominal-is-best requirements, fails for max/min-is-best (contradiction level dominates, p = 1.4e-36), and a coupled machining design can be more robust than an uncoupled one. Abstract only.
agent_test: Low priority; needs full text before use.

claim: Laypeople and engineers misjudge coupling: more than 80% of over 100 software engineers called the two-knob faucet uncoupled. Coupling is a property of the FR-DP map, not of visible parts.
agent_test: Ask the agent to classify FR-DP matrices (diagonal/triangular/coupled) from text designs; compare accuracy with a program computing it from an explicit matrix.

claim: Writing requirements well (solution-neutral FRs, one need per FR) is the most error-prone AD step; this is argued, not measured. Gap search: Homay 2507.09599 has no LLM experiment; O'Hara 2025 detected solution-jumping in 6 antipatterns (100%) but did not measure final design quality.
agent_test: Have the agent restate the task as solution-neutral requirements before solving vs not; score on tasks with framing traps.

claim: LLM extraction of FR and DP from text is hard: 6,000 patent sentences, two-expert F1 only 0.52 (FR) to 0.80 (Action); 41.33% of sentences contain neither FR nor DP; fine-tuned encoders beat prompted LLMs (gap up to 0.1 F1 on classification).
agent_test: Do not rely on the model to label FR/DP unaided; use explicit slots plus a program consistency check. Annotator agreement bounds any LLM score.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A code verifier plus a typed spec of rules lifts LLM CAD assembly success (AssemCAD 89.17/87.50 vs GPT-5.5 79.17/66.67, Claude-4.8 85.00/0.83). The 62 'axioms' are engineering rules, not Suh's.
agent_test: Name clash; cite only as support for typed spec plus verifier, not for Suh. Test: add a rule-check step at equal tokens.

claim: AD-style decomposition yields checkable invariants: SWaT 8 FRs to 44 concrete FRs; two invariants detected both attacks with no false positives (decision tree 100% on both, naive Bayes 100% and 93.75%).
agent_test: Example of an FR/DP trace turned into machine checks. Only two invariants, so weak.

claim: LLMs can fill design structure matrices at moderate accuracy: Auto-DSM reproduced 357/462 (77.3%) entries, correctness 40.0% to 82.6% by source, and plain ChatGPT scored 66.7 to 85.7%, so the workflow did not clearly beat a direct prompt.
agent_test: Test agent matrix-building from text against a gold matrix; check that program-side checks add value over a plain prompt.

claim: An LLM plus a search loop optimises DSM clustering and sequencing close to simulated annealing (Claude-Sonnet-4.6 within 1.3% on Kodak, Brake, HeatEx; 3 models x 5 cases x 10 trials); GPT and Qwen vary more run to run.
agent_test: Model of LLM proposes, program scores. Same-lab authors, so independence is partial.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Injected domain knowledge can hurt: for Claude on the two larger DSM cases (HeatEx 17 nodes, Helicopter 19) knowledge cost 5.4% and 3.6% gap, and 0 of 10 Helicopter runs hit the SA reference vs 10 of 10 without. Authors attribute it to semantic misalignment (untested hypothesis). For GPT and Qwen knowledge helps early and k=0 catches up later, so it is not a general effect of guidance.
agent_test: Test knowledge injection on vs off per task size at equal tokens; keep knowledge optional.

claim: Matrix input representation matters little (directed list, matrix, prose similar) but an undirected edge list is clearly worse.
agent_test: Keep dependency direction explicit in any scaffold matrix.

claim: Claims that AD-constrained agentic AI design cut coupling 34.2% and iterations 41% rest on an SSRN abstract by the framework authors; the abstract attributes the numbers to a separate self-cited work (Joshi 2026a), defines no coupling measure, and the full text is blocked. Unverified.
agent_test: Do not use until full text is read.

claim: No measured LLM test of Suh's independence axiom itself exists in the 2020-2026 sources found; the only LLM link is Homay's 2026 argument that LLMs are weak at abduction (cited, not tested).
agent_test: Direct test: matrix-first design vs free design on multi-requirement tasks, scoring requirement conflicts, at equal tokens.

claim: Use of the information axiom is mostly fuzzy multi-criteria selection; no outcome test of whether it picks better designs was found.

Coupling can be scored finer than the three AD classes, and one simulation of a real manufacturing information system (Mollajan 2022) reports better performance when independence is satisfied; both rest on abstracts, simulation, and advocate authors.
agent_test: Use a program-computed coupling count rather than a three-way label when checking an agent's design.

claim: Whether LLMs gain from a matrix-first scaffold, show the 3.4^n blowup on coupled numeric tuning, or can classify coupling from text were all searched again (Crossref, about 12 queries) with no study found; search tools were throttled, so these three stay open.
agent_test: Run the three tests directly: matrix-first vs free design; coupled vs uncoupled tuning n=2..5 with and without a linear solve; classification of 50 designs against a program-computed matrix.

claim: The size of the knowledge penalty in LLM modularization tracks task size and model strength, so a scaffold that adds guidance should be tested per task size and model, and scored on final quality as well as early progress.
agent_test: Ablate each guidance block (hints, examples, domain notes) on small and large tasks; log early and final score.
